title: doctor's gate-not-running finding says commits go through ungated and that no verb repairs it, and both are false
body:
Found by dc on 2026-09-24 driving `intent/docs/pre-commit-hook.md` for the 3.2.1 doc audit, in a scratch project on the pair at `4c687eaad`.

Seen: with the gate's carrier removed, `intent doctor` exits 1 with a gate-not-running finding (`finding.rs:654`) that says "commits are going through ungated ... NO VERB CURRENTLY REPAIRS THIS". Both halves are false as built: `git commit` is REFUSED (rc 1, "pre-commit: GATE ABSENT -- the Intent gate did NOT run"), and `intent claude upgrade --apply --skip-settings` repairs it -- it printed "written: .git/hooks/pre-commit.intent", after which doctor exited 0 with no gate-not-running finding.

Expected: the finding says what happens to a commit and names the verb that repairs it.

Disposition: hv's, asked on 2026-09-24: a remedy that misdirects -- it tells the reader nothing repairs what one verb repairs -- inside the shipping-grade test of hv decision 33 (1), and a one-string fix.

Re-sized by cc from the code on 2026-09-24, not yet driven: this is not a one-string fix. `finding.rs:654`'s class remedy is one string shared by three gate states (`doctor::gate_state`), each with its own detail in `doctor.rs`'s `hook_findings`, and the three are not alike. For `ChainCallsAMissingCarrier` (dc's case) the detail also says "every guard it would have run is silently skipped on every commit", while the commit is REFUSED (driven, rc 1). For `CarrierRunsNoGuards`, a monolithic carrier with no runner, "ungated" is probably true, and `intent claude upgrade --apply` repairs it by replacing the carrier (`canon::install_carrier`, `write_if_changed`). For `NoResolvableInstall`, `upgrade --apply` needs the same install root doctor failed to resolve, so the remedy there is the shim's own, `intent bootstrap`, which needs driving. Two comments state the old premise: `doctor.rs`'s "No verb repairs any of it" and `canon.rs`'s "never writes the carrier". The honest size is S: one detail per state, one remedy per state, the two comments, and one arm per state.


Driven by ic on 2026-09-24 on the pair at `4c687eaad`, in a scratch project under an isolated HOME, across every state with the install pointer good and bad; cc's re-size stands at S and is corrected in three places.

- `ChainCallsAMissingCarrier`: the commit is REFUSED ("GATE ABSENT") and `intent claude upgrade --apply` writes the carrier back; doctor then exits 0. Driven as dc drove it.
- `CarrierRunsNoGuards`: the one state where commits go through with no guard run. `upgrade --apply` replaces the carrier with the shim. With the pointer absent the shim it installs refuses every commit, upgrade itself says `remedy: intent bootstrap`, and after `intent bootstrap` the commit runs every guard. So its remedy is the upgrade, then bootstrap where the pointer names no install.
- `NoResolvableInstall` is not one state. **Doctor read the templates from the root its own binary belongs to, while the shim execs the root the install pointer names**, so doctor run from a copy of the pair outside any install, and from an install with no hook templates, reported the gate as unable to run while the pointer named this tree and every commit ran every guard (rc 0). That is a false finding, not a misworded one. With the pointer absent, the shim refuses every commit and `intent bootstrap` from a complete install repairs it; bootstrap from a binary outside any install fails with `InstallError::NotFound` and its own remedy, "reinstall Intent". With the pointer naming an install that has no `lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh`, the shim refuses and names reinstalling there, or bootstrapping from a complete install.
- The stale premises are `finding.rs`'s comment on the class remedy ("`upgrade --apply` ... never writes the carrier"), `doctor.rs`'s "No verb repairs any of it" section on `hook_findings`, and `canon.rs`'s doc on `install_carrier`, which says the chain block has no `else` and passes every commit; it has refused since the GATE ABSENT arm. It is not a `canon.rs` comment that says "never writes the carrier".

The build: one detail per state and pointer state from a pure function, the class remedy saying the detail names the consequence and the verb, the shim's template read from the root `install::gate_resolution` names, the install error and an unreadable template carried into the detail instead of dropped by `.ok()`, and the three comments. One arm per state.


Fixed at `ecb8f52eb`, landed on 2026-09-24 on vc's word; ships in 3.2.1.
